transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can’t seem to stay focused on what I’m doing at the machines long enough to do the job the way they need me to. It's starting to cause some major issues for me at the factory, and I really need to figure out what's going on.

Have you had trouble paying attention and staying organized since you were a child, or did this start more recently? Also, do you notice feeling very down or very worried when the focus problems happen?

Honestly, I’ve been like this since elementary school—I was always getting in trouble for wandering around the classroom and talking nonstop, but it became a major crisis about 14 months ago when our plant upgraded to faster machines. I don’t really feel deeply down or highly anxious when it happens, just incredibly stressed and frustrated because I’m scared of losing my job.
Do these attention and restlessness problems also affect you outside of work, like at home, when driving, or in conversations? Can you give one or two examples?

Yes, it definitely affects me at home and in conversations. On my days off, I can't just sit quietly to watch a show or read because I'm constantly getting up, fiddling with my phone, or talking over the TV since staying still feels impossible. I also tend to talk nonstop and constantly cut people off mid-sentence when we're chatting.
